purpose: Estimate whether an individual profile is likely to be financially included and likely to use mobile money.

financial_inclusion.question: Based on the characteristics provided, is this person likely to be financially included?
financial_inclusion.answer: This person is unlikely to be financially included.

main_factors.label: education level
main_factors.explanation: Education level (Primary education or less) reduced the prediction relative to the model baseline.

main_factors.label: workforce status
main_factors.explanation: Workforce status (Out of the workforce) reduced the prediction relative to the model baseline.

main_factors.label: age group
main_factors.explanation: Age group (65+) increased the prediction relative to the model baseline.

main_factors.label: recent internet use
main_factors.explanation: Recent internet use (No / don't know / refused) reduced the prediction relative to the model baseline.

main_factors.label: income quintile
main_factors.explanation: Income quintile (Income quintile 2) reduced the prediction relative to the model baseline.

mobile_money_adoption.question: Based on the characteristics provided, is this person likely to use mobile money?
mobile_money_adoption.answer: This person is unlikely to use mobile money.

main_factors.label: internet engagement
main_factors.explanation: Internet engagement (No recent internet use / no-DK-ref) reduced the prediction relative to the model baseline.

main_factors.label: education level
main_factors.explanation: Education level (Primary education or less) reduced the prediction relative to the model baseline.

main_factors.label: SIM registration in own name
main_factors.explanation: Sim registration in own name (Yes) increased the prediction relative to the model baseline.

main_factors.label: data-purchase pattern
main_factors.explanation: Data-purchase pattern (No recent internet use / skipped) reduced the prediction relative to the model baseline.

main_factors.label: income quintile
main_factors.explanation: Income quintile (Income quintile 2) reduced the prediction relative to the model baseline.

disclaimer: This proof-of-concept explains model predictions, not causation, eligibility, creditworthiness, or an official World Bank classification.
